title: A Memorial Is Proposed at the Precise Martyrdom Site

blocks.text: Episode 152 continues by describing how the aftermath of the Sahibzadas' killing lingers as an affliction in Muslim memory and local conscience. Ordinary consolations fail, and the narrative pushes toward a remedy that acknowledges the sanctity of the place where the crime was committed.

The solution offered is explicit: a memorial be built at the precise place where the Guru's sons were put to death. The page imagines the site not as abandoned ground but as a kept, illuminated, and attended place of reverence.
In this way the memorial becomes both historical witness and devotional practice. The city that carried the stain of the killing is asked to preserve the very location it once tried to erase.
